blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: Rewrite `bucket` as a plain function a newcomer can read without the plan: name the threshold as a constant in cents (e.g. `PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`) and compare `p.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS` instead of the bit trick `(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8`, which a reader cannot translate into a price boundary (and which, read literally, tests bits rather than a threshold, so the shape hides what the rule really does); replace the comma-operator reduce with `||=` mutation by a loop or two `filter` calls; give the result an explicit type (`{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }`) with both keys always present, instead of `Record<string, Price[]>` with the magic keys "hi"/"lo" that the doc comment calls "cheap" and "premium"; and use descriptive names (`prices`, `price`, `groups`) instead of `ps`, `a`, `p`, and a verb such as `splitByPriceTier` instead of `bucket`.
findings.title: `bucket` packs its grouping rule into an unreadable one-liner
